title: Locate the quantity and unit
context: Three air filters were tested under the same inlet dust concentration. The table separates outlet dust from airflow.

title: Distinguish totals, changes, and fractions
context: A treatment starts with 60 mg/L solute and finishes with 15 mg/L; water volume is unchanged.

title: Check simultaneous constraints
context: Use the same three air filters; the specification requires both sufficient airflow and sufficiently low outlet dust.

title: Normalize unequal sample sizes
context: Two differently sized quadrats were surveyed using the same counting method.

title: Read points, changes, and slopes
context: Two seedling groups are measured on the same days. These are heights, not growth rates.

title: Combine data with matched units and weights
context: Two steady streams combine without pollutant gain or loss and mix uniformly.

title: Link calibrations, dilution, and a new condition
context: A sensor reports a linear signal of 3 units per mg/L for the diluted sample. Dilution factor = 4; original-stream water flow = 2 L/s.

title: Compare rates over the actual intervals
context: A sealed vial cools in a room maintained below all listed vial temperatures.

title: Interpolate with the nearest bounding values
context: Assume the temperature varies linearly between the two measured points for this estimate.

title: Limit peaks and trends to tested conditions
context: An enzyme is measured under identical conditions except for temperature.

title: Keep slope, intercept, and units separate
context: A pressure model applies over the listed depth range.

title: Use nonlinear models when requested
context: The model x = 3√t describes a spreading front during the tested interval.

title: Read turning points and limits separately
context: Measurements were taken at equal exposure intervals below the detector limit of 100 units.

title: Carry new information through the whole model
context: Daily growth is additive; a temporary treatment changes only Day 3.

title: Name variables and controls precisely
context: Separate matched plants receive one fertilizer dose each; all plants are measured on Day 12.

title: Detect confounds and isolate the treatment
context: The comparison is intended to test temperature, but the initial water source differs.

title: Match the comparison to the hypothesis
context: Time is recorded until 30 mL of gas has formed under identical reaction conditions.

title: Count independent experimental units
context: Salinity is assigned to whole tanks; fish within each tank share the same water.

title: Separate randomization, blinding, and carryover
context: A behavior trial assigns insects to one tone exposure and records each response.

title: Use a two-factor comparison and test interactions
context: A factorial study uses separate matched organisms at each combination of light and feeding.

title: Check measurement definitions, precision, and accuracy
context: A reference bath has accepted temperature 50.0°C; the same thermometer takes three readings.

title: Map each proposed cause to its prediction
context: Two researchers explain the same pale appearance; the filter removes clay particles but does not remove dissolved salt.

title: Control the competing explanation
context: Cloudiness is measured under matched lighting and constant salt concentration.

title: Distinguish feasibility, necessity, and history
context: The study tests survival during transport, not which route happened during the original colonization.

title: Use the same condition for competing predictions
context: Both viewpoints predict a higher color score under their proposed driving condition.

title: Choose tests where predictions diverge
context: Organisms are tested in a chamber in which the two proposed cues can be positioned independently.

title: Test required conditions and detection limits
context: All relevant conditions other than salt meet the model’s stated conditions.

title: Test a complex claim one requirement at a time
context: Matched growth trials independently vary light and iron.

title: Compute predictions from the exact rule
context: The models describe extension x in cm for force F in N, within 0–4 N.

title: Separate additive and multiplicative change
context: A model assumes unlimited resources over the measured 0–6 h interval.

title: Respect the model’s domain
context: The model applies to one material and only the listed input interval.

title: Apply simultaneous factor changes with units
context: The model applies over the proposed changes; k is constant.

title: Correct the baseline before testing the pattern
context: Measurements are equally spaced and the corrected signal halves each interval.

title: Separate saturation from unlimited growth
context: Both models apply for positive C in the proposed test range.

title: Combine evidence and choose an informative follow-up
context: Independent matched groups are measured for the same duration at both light and nutrient levels.

title: Acidity, enzymes, and concentration
context: The enzyme is tested at a constant temperature while solution pH is varied.

title: Atoms, ions, reactions, and conserved matter
context: The reaction occurs in a sealed vessel; all matter, including leftover gas, remains inside.

title: Force, density, and electrical relationships
context: Both forces act along one horizontal line; other horizontal forces are negligible.

title: Cells, photosynthesis, and net measurements
context: Equal leaf samples are measured for one hour; assume respiration has the same rate in light and dark.

title: Heat, phase changes, and energy
context: Heater power is constant and losses are negligible for the comparison.

title: Inheritance and population proportions
context: The trait follows one-gene complete dominance and equal gamete probabilities.

title: Waves and supplied physical models
context: Both waves travel through the same unchanged medium with speed 24 m/s.

title: Earth, space, and relative evidence
context: The layers are undisturbed and upright before the stated fault forms.
